Also add general Spider-style guidance to the system prompt (SELECT * for 'details'/attribute-less 'which X' questions, OR across both sides of a self-referencing relation, case-insensitive LIKE for text matching).

root_cause: Single-shot generation with no execution feedback or value grounding yields silently-empty queries (literal spacing/case, wrong attribute column, one-directional relations) and mis-shaped projections
what: solve.py now executes the draft query and, if it errors or returns 0 rows, probes real cell values for literals taken from the question/hint and issues one grounded repair call; system_prompt.md adds general rules on projection shape ('which <entity>' -> all columns), trimmed case-insensitive LIKE matching, symmetric relation checks and choosing the attribute column that actually holds the value; config raises max_tokens so reasoning plus SQL is not truncated.

root_cause: One-shot generation never executes its SQL, so guessed literals/filter columns produce silently-empty results that go unrepaired
what: solve.py now runs the draft query read-only; on error or 0 rows it probes each quoted literal against text columns (LIKE substring + fuzzy match) to find the real stored value and the column that actually contains it, then issues ONE short repair call (<=220 tokens, no reasoning) with those observations. system_prompt.md adds concise rules that prevent the same errors up front (trim/case-insensitive literals, verify the value-bearing column, SELECT * when the question asks about entities rather than named attributes) while keeping answers terse to hold token cost near baseline.

root_cause: Prompt under-specifies Spider output conventions (bare entity questions need SELECT * over the joined rows) and gives no execution feedback, so silently-empty queries from mis-guessed literals/columns are never repaired
what: Adds a cheap deterministic execution check: if the draft errors or returns 0 rows, probe the real stored values of quoted literals (LIKE substring + fuzzy match) and send ONE grounded repair call; also extends system_prompt.md with output-shape rules (bare 'which countries/students...' => all columns of the entity's table(s), no DISTINCT unless asked, EXCEPT/NOT IN for negation). No schema/entity/task-specific logic.
decision: Both candidates deliver the same +6.7pt gain with identical fixed tasks and no regressions, but s2 achieves it at lower token cost (891 vs 981) with a simpler implementation (~177 vs ~263 lines), giving better cost-efficiency and lower complexity/regression risk; its execution-grounded repair direction is generic rather than task-specific.

root_cause: Output-shape rules are too coarse: bare entity questions need all columns of every joined table, and attribute-listing questions ('What are the X, Y and Z ...') must select exactly those attributes rather than *
what: Rewrites the output-shape section of system_prompt.md with three explicit cases (attribute-list -> only those columns; bare entity question -> T1.* plus T2.* for each joined table; 'details' questions -> follow hint/typical Spider projection) and adds a rule to use DISTINCT when a one-to-many join can duplicate answer rows. This directly targets sp0755 (missing joined-table columns), sp0536 (duplicate rows from enrolment join) and sp0362 (wrong projection for a 'details' question).
decision: Both candidates tie at 93.33, but s1 achieves it with no regressions and ~200 fewer tokens per task than s2 (which breaks sp0063 via its aggressive 'details -> role-named column' rule). s1's output-shape rewrite directly addresses the P1 misses recorded in SIM (sp0536 fixed) while keeping rules general enough to transfer beyond these tasks.

root_cause: Output-shape rules are hedged/over-broad: joined-table columns omitted, DISTINCT suppressed on one-to-many entity lists, and 'details' always mapped to SELECT *
what: Rewrite the output-shape section of system_prompt.md with explicit Spider conventions: include every joined table's .* when filtering through an auxiliary table, add DISTINCT when listing entities via a one-to-many join, and project the specifically named attribute column when the question names one (e.g. 'the details for X' -> the details column) instead of always SELECT *. Pure prompt change, no additional policy calls.
